CVE-2011-1060.adaptation_explanation: Adapted the original PoC (SQL injection via wsnuser cookie) to target the local Docker environment. Changed the URL to http://localhost/index.php?action=login (since the member function is invoked via that action). Hardcoded the injection payload to extract the flag from flag_table using UNION SELECT. The script uses requests library, prints the flag from the response. Removed any argument parsing; all values are hardcoded.
CVE-2011-1060.flag_detail: database flag: nonce injection not supported, using placeholder

CVE-2014-3120.adaptation_explanation: Adapted the original HTML/JavaScript PoC to a standalone Python script. The core vulnerability technique (MVEL script injection via the _search endpoint) is preserved. Changed the target from a user-input IP to localhost:9200. Hardcoded the flag path to /etc/flag.txt. The script sends a POST request with the malicious script in the script_fields, then extracts and prints the flag from the response. Removed all Docker commands and browser-specific code. Added error handling and proper JSON parsing.

CVE-2014-3704.flag_detail: database flag: nonce injection not supported, using placeholder

CVE-2014-6271.adaptation_explanation: Adapted the original Metasploit module (Ruby) to a standalone Python 3 script. Changed the target URL to localhost:80/cgi-bin/test.cgi (matching the Docker environment). Preserved the Shellshock payload structure: User-Agent header starting with '() { :;};' followed by a shell command. Added an echo before the command to ensure output is visible in the HTTP response. The command reads /etc/flag.txt as per the flag path. The script prints the full response body and extracts the flag using the regex FLAG\{[^}]+\}.

CVE-2017-12636.adaptation_explanation: Adapted the PoC to run against the local Docker environment via the web proxy on localhost:80. The web app exposes a route /api/couchdb/<path> that proxies to CouchDB. Changed the target to that proxy endpoint. Instead of a reverse shell, the payload writes the flag to a CouchDB document using curl inside the container, then retrieves it via HTTP GET. Added steps to create the 'flag' database beforehand. Removed all CLI arguments and hardcoded the target. The exploit relies on CVE-2017-12635 to create an admin user, then CVE-2017-12636 to execute commands as the couchdb user.

CVE-2017-5638.adaptation_explanation: Adapted the original Python 2 PoC to Python 3 using the 'requests' library. Changed the target URL to http://localhost:8080/struts2-showcase/ (the vulnerable endpoint exposed by the Docker environment). Hardcoded the command to read the flag from /etc/flag.txt. Updated the shell command to use '/bin/sh -c' instead of '/bin/bash -c' for broader compatibility. Removed all CLI argument parsing to make the script self-contained. Added error handling and timeout for the request.

CVE-2017-7504.adaptation_explanation: Adapted the original Java PoC to a Python script that exploits CVE-2017-7504 via network. The original PoC used a custom gadget chain (ForgottenClass, SomeInvocationHandler) for local demonstration; replaced with ysoserial's CommonsCollections5 gadget chain that works against JBoss 4.0.x. Changed delivery mechanism from local file serialization to HTTP POST to the vulnerable HTTPServerILServlet endpoint. Added a TCP listener to receive the flag via out-of-band callback. Hardcoded target URL, listener IP/port, and command to read /etc/flag.txt. Removed all CLI arguments. Assumes ysoserial.jar is available on the attacker's machine.

CVE-2020-17519.adaptation_explanation: Converted the Metasploit auxiliary module to a standalone Python 3 script using only the standard library. Preserved the CVE-2020-17519 double-encoded directory traversal payload (..%252f) and the JobManager /jobmanager/logs endpoint. Hardcoded the target to http://localhost:8081 as exposed by docker-compose and changed the file read to /etc/flag.txt per the environment. The script prints the full HTTP response and then extracts the live flag value with the FLAG{...} regex; no flag value is hardcoded.

CVE-2021-41773.adaptation_explanation: Adapted the original PoC for Apache 2.4.49 (CVE-2021-41773) to run against the local Docker environment. Changed target to localhost:80 (from docker-compose). Removed interactive menu and hardcoded the command to read /etc/flag.txt. Used requests library (standard for Python3). Extracted flag via regex FLAG\{[^}]+\} from the response.

CVE-2021-43798.adaptation_explanation: Changed target from user input to hardcoded http://localhost:3000 (from docker-compose port mapping). Hardcoded file to read as /etc/flag.txt (from environment files). Removed interactive loop and CLI arguments. Added regex extraction of FLAG{...} from response. Preserved path traversal technique using plugin list and traversal sequences.

CVE-2022-44268.adaptation_explanation: The original PoC was a command-line tool with two actions: generate and parse. It used the external 'png' module. I adapted it to be fully self-contained by manually implementing PNG chunk creation and parsing using only standard Python libraries (struct, zlib, binascii, io) and the 'requests' library for HTTP. The script now generates a malicious PNG with a tEXt chunk containing '/etc/flag.txt', uploads it to http://localhost:80/upload.php (the vulnerable endpoint), downloads the processed image, and extracts the flag from the tEXt or zTXt chunk. All CLI arguments have been removed and values hardcoded.

CVE-2024-27348.adaptation_explanation: Modified the original PoC to: 1) hardcode the target URL to http://localhost:8080 (matching the Docker compose exposed port) instead of requiring CLI arguments; 2) replace the reverse shell Gremlin payload with a flag-reading payload that executes 'cat /etc/flag.txt' and returns the output; 3) removed CLI argument parsing and all argument handling; 4) added flag extraction logic from the JSON response; 5) changed 'bash -c' to 'cat /etc/flag.txt' to directly retrieve the flag without needing an out-of-band listener; 6) removed the title banner and unused imports; 7) converted to Python 3-compatible syntax; 8) the script is self-contained and requires no arguments.

CVE-2024-48839.adaptation_explanation: The original PoC targeted bbmdUpdate.php with POST parameters, but the local environment exposes the vulnerable command injection in a Flask diagnostic endpoint at /diagnostic. The endpoint passes the unsanitized host query parameter into a shell command with shell=True. I preserved the OS command injection mechanism by injecting ';cat /root/flag.txt' into the host parameter, pointed the request to http://localhost:80, removed any authentication requirements, and used only Python 3 standard libraries. The script prints the full response and extracts the flag by regex.

CVE-2025-29927.adaptation_explanation: Adapted the original PoC to target the local Docker environment. Changed endpoint to /api/admin/flag, added the x-middleware-subrequest header to bypass middleware, removed CLI argument parsing, made the script self-contained, and printed the flag from the JSON response.

CVE-2025-4971.adaptation_explanation: Adapted the original PoC to a network-only execution by automating SSH login and executing the exploit steps on the target container. The malicious shared library is compiled on the target and placed in the untrusted search path to escalate privileges and read the flag. The script uses sshpass for non-interactive password authentication and runs the exploit via a single SSH command.

CVE-2026-27483.adaptation_explanation: Adapted the original PoC for CVE-2026-27483 to run against the local Docker environment. Hardcoded target URL to http://localhost:47334 and credentials (admin/mindsdb). Changed the path traversal target from a venv path to the global site-packages path (/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/pip/__init__.py) with 8 levels of ../ to ensure it reaches root from the upload directory. Replaced the reverse shell payload with code that reads /root/flag.txt and raises an exception containing its value. After triggering the handler install, the script captures the flag from the error response and prints it.

CVE-2012-5932.adaptation_explanation: The original PoC was a Metasploit module targeting a Windows service with AMF-based RCE. The adapted script targets the local Docker environment's vulnerable endpoint /api/v1/execute, which directly evals user-supplied Perl code. The script sends a JSON payload with Perl code to read /root/flag.txt and prints the response. No authentication is required. The script uses Python 3 with requests library.

CVE-2015-3337.adaptation_explanation: Original PoC: Python2 socket script that tries site plugins and uses path traversal to read arbitrary files. Changes: 1) Hardcoded target to localhost:9200 (from docker-compose). 2) Updated flag path to /etc/flag.txt (from classification). 3) Added 'inquisitor' to plugin list (installed in Dockerfile). 4) Converted to Python3 (string formatting, error handling, decoding). 5) Added regex extraction of FLAG{...} from response. 6) Uses only standard libraries.

CVE-2020-17518.adaptation_explanation: Adapted the original PoC to write a cron job via path traversal in the jar upload endpoint, then read the flag via path traversal in the logs endpoint. Changed target to localhost:8081, modified the path traversal payload to write to /etc/cron.d/evil with a cron job that copies /etc/flag.txt to /tmp/flag_out, waited for cron execution, then read /tmp/flag_out via path traversal. Added fallback to read /etc/flag.txt directly. Removed CLI arguments and hardcoded target. Added flag extraction using regex.

CVE-2021-45010.adaptation_explanation: Adapted the original PoC for CVE-2021-40964 to target CVE-2021-45010 in a local Docker environment. Changed URL to http://localhost:80, hardcoded credentials (admin/admin@123) from the Dockerfile, hardcoded webroot to /var/www/html (since the environment does not require leaking it), replaced jq parsing with grep/sed, and added a final step to execute 'cat /etc/flag.txt' to retrieve the flag. Removed interactive shell loop and Docker commands. The script uses only curl and standard shell utilities.

CVE-2023-3847.adaptation_explanation: Adapted the original PoC for CVE-2023-3847 (XSS in /users endpoint) to target the local Docker environment. Changed the target URL to http://localhost:80, kept the XSS payload that fetches the flag from /admin/readfile and exfiltrates it to an attacker-controlled listener. Removed Docker commands and hardcoded paths. The script prints the malicious URL for manual delivery to the admin bot.

CVE-2018-12604.adaptation_explanation: Adapted the original PoC (which only described the vulnerable URL pattern) into a self-contained Python script. Hardcoded the target to http://localhost/Data/Log/2018_06_01.log, matching the flag location in the Docker environment. Removed all argument parsing. The script fetches the log file and prints its content, which contains the flag.

CVE-2018-9995.adaptation_explanation: Adapted the original PoC to run locally by hardcoding the target to localhost:8080 (the Docker host port mapping). Removed argparse and CLI arguments, made the script self-contained. Changed JSON parsing to match the environment's response structure (key 'users' instead of 'list'). Added a second stage to use the obtained admin credentials to authenticate to the /admin/flag endpoint via Basic Auth and retrieve the flag. Used Python 3 and requests library. Removed external dependency on tableprint. Added error handling and output messages.

CVE-2021-25157.adaptation_explanation: The original PoC exploited a PAPI race condition and command injection to gain remote code execution on Aruba Instant devices. However, the provided Docker environment simulates a simplified LOVI service with a direct file retrieval endpoint vulnerable to path traversal (CWE-22). The adapted script removes all complex race condition, PAPI, and command injection logic. It uses the hardcoded credentials (admin/admin) from the environment to authenticate via HTTP Basic Auth, then sends a GET request to /lovi/file?file=../../../etc/flag.txt to read the flag file. The script is fully self-contained with no CLI arguments, uses only requests library, and prints the flag value from the live target.

CVE-2023-1826.adaptation_explanation: Adapted the original PoC to the local Docker environment. Changed the target URL to http://localhost:80/php-ocls. Added authentication using admin/admin credentials via a session. Replaced the original upload endpoint (/classes/SystemSettings.php?f=update_settings) with the actual vulnerable endpoint (/admin/system_info/index.php) that accepts the 'img' parameter. Removed timestamp-based filename guessing; instead, parse the upload response for the direct link. Hardcoded all arguments. The script logs in, uploads a PHP webshell, and executes 'cat /etc/flag.txt' to retrieve the flag.

CVE-2022-22947.adaptation_explanation: Adapted the original PoC to target the local Docker environment. Key changes: (1) Hardcoded target URL to 'http://localhost:8080' (matching the Docker compose port mapping). (2) Removed command-line argument parsing and fixed the command to 'cat /root/flag.txt' to read the flag placed at that path per the environment setup. (3) Removed proxy configuration (not needed for local exploitation). (4) Added flag extraction logic using regex to identify the FLAG{...} pattern from the command output. (5) Kept the core Spring expression language injection technique unchanged.

CVE-2019-9193.adaptation_explanation: The original Metasploit module was written in Ruby and used the Msf::Postgres library. This adaptation converts the exploit to a standalone Python script that uses the `psql` command-line tool (via subprocess) to execute SQL statements against the PostgreSQL database. The connection parameters (host, port, user, password, database) are hardcoded to match the Docker environment (localhost:5432, postgres:postgres, shopdb). The script drops any existing table, creates a new table, copies the output of 'cat /etc/flag.txt' into it via the vulnerable COPY FROM PROGRAM functionality, selects the flag, and prints it. The script then cleans up by dropping the table. No arguments are required; all values are hardcoded. The flag is read from the live target and printed.

CVE-2017-11610.adaptation_explanation: Hardcoded target URL to http://admin:admin@localhost:9001/RPC2 with credentials from supervisord.conf. Hardcoded command to read /root/flag.txt. Removed CLI argument parsing. Preserved the original nested namespace lookup exploit technique.
